sentences.text: Prosecution story, in brief, is that, at the time of the incident, the prosecutrix was aged about 16 years and 04 months.
From one month ago to the incident, the prosecutrix was known to the co-accused Govind and there was telephonic conversation between both of them.
On 15.05.2023, at around 11:30 PM.
After calling co-accused Govind, the prosecutrix met him at Balaji Temple.
The co-accused Govind took the prosecutrix in a Jungle.
The present applicant and co-accused Devilal had followed them by another motorcycle.
Co-accused Govind asked the prosecutrix that whether she wants to marry him, she replied that she is ready to marry him.

Thereafter, the co-accused Govind had forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her, while she was denying and thereafter,
he also denied to marry her.
On the same night, at around 04:30 AM, the prosecutrix returned home and narrated the incident to her maternal uncle.
On 16.05.2023, the prosecutrix reported the matter at Police Station Ratangarh, District Neemuch.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant/accused has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.
Learned counsel submits that as per allegations, the present applicant had not committed sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix.
He is in custody since 18.05.2023.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.
The trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that present applicant/accused be released on bail.
5. On the other hand, learned Government Advocate for the non- applicant/State has objected the prayer and prayed for its rejection.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail, hence, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant - Shankarlal @ Kaleshwar Shankar shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) alongwith one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Court, for his appearance before the concerned Court regularly on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
9. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE Shruti Shankarlal @ Kaleshwer Shankar Bhil vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144514201/
